interpretation: Two MX49 brackets per low-speed brake and two MX47 per track brake: eight total. Opposite half-band occurrences reuse each bracket definition by rigid rotation.
One lateral lug per bracket alternates across the band width, with a single M348 or M353 pin also passing through the inboard M337 link. This hidden joint is an estimated reconstruction.

SNL half-band assemblies place low-speed retainers on lower-left/upper-right and track retainers on upper-left/lower-right halves. Opposite transverse lug directions for MX49/MX47 make these retainers consistently outboard in this hypothesis.

Rear split half-gap increases from1 to4degrees to receive the anchor joint. Printed segment lengths and source hole spacing stay unchanged; each half-band and its lining/rivet pattern advances3degrees toward the front.

Rear feet cover two existing copper lining rivets per half-band. Those16 rivets use SNL quarter-inch x1-3/8 stock instead of1-1/8 stock, matching the estimated6.35mm added grip. Later strip-variant counts are not imposed on the earlier segmented lining.

SNL191 specifies8 steel3/8 x1-3/8 countersunk rivets per MX49 and7 per MX47, giving60 at the rear. SNL167 additionally lists three quarter-inch button rivets for MX49; application/count conflict remains open.

HB156 describes coupling set screws after anchor-pin removal. SNL lists MX38/MX60/MX76 screw families but does not unambiguously locate them on this low/track joint. The simple interleaved-lug hypothesis does not prove that service sequence. No unspecified coupling screw is silently added or called installed.
